messages:
Harper (AM): starting Silverline POC thread. They want Redwood Private deployed into their AWS account, need a single stable egress IP for allowlisting, and completion of the security questionnaire. POC window: 10 business days.
Ken (SE): clarifying Qs: do they require the original client IP to be visible to their downstream services (for audit logs)? Also, are they running TLS inspection on egress?
Harper (AM): downstream logging requires original client IP. TLS inspection likely in place.
Priya (NetOps): options summary:
- Fastest/cheapest: run Private in their VPC but reuse their NAT -> SNAT happens and client IP is lost.
- Preserve-client-IP: run serving inside customer VPC behind NLBs with proxy-protocol v2 OR use NLBs with EIPs and have our pods behind them. Proxy-protocol preserves source IP.
- Stable egress IPs (allowlist): provision NAT Gateway(s) with Elastic IPs in each AZ or central egress NAT behind Transit Gateway.
Sam (Solutions Eng): PrivateLink note: interface endpoints avoid peering and give stable DNS names. If they enable PrivateLink private DNS, ensure split-horizon resolution works for their corporate DNS. Example service name: com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-0abcd1234.us-west-2.
Ish (InfoSec): questionnaire blocker items: rotating egress, TLS inspection, and KMS custody. Draft attestation language: "No public inbound ports required. Outbound: HTTPS (TCP/443) to our control-plane FQDNs (e.g., *.redwood-inference.com) and to model artifact endpoints (s3.amazonaws.com or model-registry.redwood-inference.com). TLS 1.2+ enforced; mTLS available for Private deployments. Customers may use dedicated EIPs for allowlisting; customer-managed KMS (CMK) supported and KMS usage is recorded in CloudTrail for audit."
Ken (SE): curl + dns tests they can run for PrivateLink and DNS validation:
```
# verify private DNS resolves (if enabled)
dig +short model.redwood-inference.com @VPC_DNS_RESOLVER
# test endpoint
curl -v https://vpce-0abcd123.vpce-svc-zzz.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health -H 'Host: model.redwood-inference.com'
```
Priya (NetOps): firewall snippet for questionnaire (pasteable):
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to: *.redwood-inference.com (control plane)
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to: s3.amazonaws.com (model artifacts)
- Allow outbound UDP/TCP/53 to VPC resolver (if using Private DNS)
If they insist on IPs: provision NAT Gateway(s) -> allocate EIPs per AZ and share the list.
Sam (Solutions Eng): TLS-inspect caveat: corp TLS proxies that terminate TLS and re-encrypt with new certs will break hostname verification. Two mitigations: 1) request bypass for our FQDNs, or 2) enable mTLS so a proxy cannot MITM. Add to questionnaire: "Does corporate egress TLS inspection occur? If yes, allowlist our hostnames or enable mTLS."
Ish (InfoSec): KMS wording for legal: "For Private deployments we support customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS). Customers can provide CMK ARN used to encrypt model keys; KMS Generate/Decrypt calls are visible in CloudTrail. For hosted deployments, reference Redwood SOC2 report (link provided)."
Harper (AM): pricing: will dedicated NAT/EIPs add POC cost? Need a one-liner for customer.
Priya (NetOps): yes. Recommend two POC cost patterns for the quote: Minimal (reuse existing NAT -> minimal infra cost, but no client IP) vs Isolated (dedicated NAT Gateways + EIPs per AZ or NLB+EIP pattern -> infra cost). We'll add ballpark NAT Gateway hourly and per-GB charges to the quote.
Ken (SE): small config note for preserving client IP in the app logs: enable proxy-protocol v2 on the NLB and configure backend to read PROXY header or X-Forwarded-For (depending on runtime).
Sam (Solutions Eng): sample NLB snippet (for ops):
```
- Create NLB in private subnets
- Enable proxy-protocol v2 on target group
- Attach backend instances/containers
- If egress allowlist required, place NAT Gateway with EIP in each AZ or route through egress appliance with fixed EIP
```
Ish (InfoSec): add to questionnaire attestation: checkbox list they can tick:
- [ ] No inbound public ports enabled
- [ ] Outbound restricted to listed FQDNs/IPs
- [ ] TLS 1.2+ enforced or mTLS enabled
- [ ] Customer-managed KMS for Private deployment (ARN provided)
Harper (AM): action items: 1) Sam -> one-page network diagram + example curl/dig tests (ETA today). 2) Priya -> firewall rules + NAT/EIP runbook + ballpark costs (ETA EOD). 3) Ish -> final attestation snippet + cert links (ETA tomorrow). 4) Ken -> KMS/legal blurb (ETA tomorrow).
deploy-bot: POC sandbox provisioned in us-west-2 (build-2117). :rocket:
Harper (AM): thanks team 44d will send to Silverline secops tomorrow and attach diagram. Any one-liners to add?
Ken (SE): one-liner: "Control plane and model artifact traffic is over TLS 1.2+ to public FQDNs; customers can provide dedicated EIPs for allowlisting."
Ish (InfoSec): one-liner: "Private deployments support customer-managed CMKs and CloudTrail auditing of KMS calls."
Harper (AM): closing loop.
